newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Former Burundi president arrested -- radio.
newsitem.headline: Former Burundi president arrested -- radio.

text.p: Former Burundi president Jean-Baptiste Bagaza, who was ousted in a military coup in 1987, has been arrested, Radio Burundi reported on Sunday.

Bagaza was overthrown in 1987 by Burundi's present leader, Pierre Buyoya, who ruled until 1993. Buyoya seized power again last July in a military coup which has drawn international condemnation and demands for the restoration of constitutional rule.
The radio gave no reason for the arrest of Bagaza, a Tutsi. But it was a day after the arrest of another leading politician, Deo Neozima, president of the opposition party, Sojedem.
Neozima had earlier published an open letter attacking Buyoya's leadership, saying it had brought no benefits for Burundi.

Buyoya on Friday called a national debate starting on January 28 to try to end civil war in his tiny central African country. He told a news conference that not all Burundians shared the same views on how to end the fighting and he wanted to listen to the opinion of everyone.
Buyoya, a moderate Tutsi, toppled Hutu president Sylvestre Ntibantunganya -- a Hutu -- in the July 25 bloodless coup.

Burundi, like neighbouring Rwanda, was for centuries ruled by a Tutsi minority. Although a Hutu president was elected in 1993, after the introduction of multi-party politics, the Tutsi have continued to dominate the government, and especially the national army.
Hundreds of thousands of civilians, mainly Hutus, have died in violence in Burundi over the last 25 years.
The country is experiencing severe economic problems following the imposition of an economic embargo by neighbouring African states in a bid to reverse last year's coup.
